description: Acidalia Sol Ares-6 is a student engineering and design team building an AI-powered Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer set on Mars. Inspired by real NASA Martian telemetry and survival physics, our interactive simulator challenges players aged 7–12 to manage critical habitat resources—balancing oxygen generation, solar grid power, water reserves, and communication delays during extreme Martian dust storms and radiation events.
summary:
**Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer — Survive, Explore and Learn on Mars**

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive 3D educational space survival game designed primarily for children aged 7–12.
Players begin their astronaut journey at a NASA-inspired training centre, prepare for launch, travel to Mars and learn to survive on another planet.
The game introduces realistic space exploration concepts through interactive missions involving oxygen management, habitat construction, spacesuit safety, airlocks, resource conservation and Martian exploration.
Our goal is to make complex space science understandable, exciting and accessible to young learners by allowing them to experience the consequences of their decisions.
Built using Babylon.js, JavaScript and Python Flask, the project combines 3D environments, scientific research and mission-based storytelling.
The current prototype demonstrates our approach to combining education, simulation and interactive gameplay, with additional mission systems planned for future development.
details:
The Problem

Space exploration involves complex scientific and engineering challenges, including maintaining breathable air, protecting astronauts from hazardous environments, conserving resources and operating equipment safely.

Young students often learn about these challenges through textbooks and videos, with limited opportunities to experience how decisions affect an astronaut's survival.

Our Solution

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer transforms space science into an interactive 3D learning experience.

Players begin their mission at a NASA-inspired training facility, board a spacecraft and experience a journey to Mars through a guided launch and landing sequence.

Once on Mars, they must complete mission objectives, monitor survival resources and learn correct procedures for operating in a simulated extraterrestrial environment.

Main Features

Astronaut training and launch: Select an astronaut, enter the training centre and experience a mission briefing, launch sequence, space journey and landing.

Mars exploration: Explore a 3D Martian environment with lower gravity, interactive objects, exploration equipment and scientific mission activities.

Survival simulation: Manage oxygen, water, food, energy and health while responding to the challenges of living on Mars.

EVA and airlock procedures: Learn why protective suits, pressure management and safety checks are necessary when transitioning between spacecraft or habitats and the Martian environment.

Habitat and life support: Work towards constructing a temporary habitat, managing access through an airlock and using sleeping facilities.

Robotic exploration: Interact with a robotic science rover and inspect a six-wheeled Mars Racer exhibit representing a future crew transport concept.

Mission-based learning: Complete guided activities intended to develop problem-solving, scientific reasoning and decision-making skills.

Scientific Approach

The game incorporates NASA-inspired concepts such as Martian gravity, surface conditions, atmospheric hazards, astronaut safety and resource management. It simplifies some scientific processes and compresses time to make them understandable and playable for younger students.

Technologies Used

  • Babylon.js for real-time 3D graphics and scene interactions.
  • JavaScript, HTML and CSS for gameplay, user interfaces and controls.
  • Python and Flask for the local application server.
  • Blender-based 3D design and game asset workflows.
  • Git and GitHub for collaborative development and version control.
  • AI-assisted development tools for programming, debugging and asset preparation.

Current Limitations and Future Development

The prototype is under active development. Advanced crew-rover driving, multiplayer networking, additional mission scenarios and persistent mission saves are not complete. Some gameplay paths require additional end-to-end testing.

Our long-term goal is to develop a more complete, accessible astronaut training experience that can support science education through interactive missions, exploration and realistic decision-making.
